# Opportunities

| name | summary |
|---|---|
| [Agent ambassadors between player worlds](agent-ambassadors-async.md) | Let each player's simulation send language-agent representatives that trade and negotiate with other players' worlds while they are offline. |
| [AI liquidity in player markets](ai-liquidity-in-player-markets.md) | Keep player-driven markets liquid on small servers with model-driven traders whose behavior is calibrated to human trading and constrained by market rules. |
| [Automated mechanic discovery](mechanic-discovery-search.md) | Search the space of rule programs with language-model-guided evolution and agent playtests to propose new mechanics that are learnable, deep, and unlike existing ones. |
| [Bottleneck explainer for production networks](bottleneck-explainer.md) | Explain where and why a production network is starved or blocked by combining sensitivity analysis of the actual simulation with grounded language explanations. |
| [Branch preview of policy futures](branch-preview-forecasts.md) | Fork the simulation in the background and show the player likely futures of a decision before committing, using parallel or surrogate simulation. |
| [Calibrated serious simulations](calibrated-serious-sims.md) | Use simulation-based inference and differentiable simulators to calibrate game-grade models of epidemics, traffic, and markets to real data, with published fit metrics. |
| [Content-elastic event systems](content-elastic-events.md) | Remove the authoring ceiling on event chains, requests, and dilemmas by generating schema-constrained variants from designer templates and validating them against game state. |
| [Drama-aware storyteller](drama-aware-storyteller.md) | A storyteller that models characters' arcs and relationships, not only threat budgets, choosing authored incidents that create meaningful stakes for specific colonists. |
| [Event-sourced simulation runtime](event-sourced-sim-runtime.md) | An engine layer that records simulation and model calls as an append-only event log, giving replay, forking, explanation, and determinism for games with AI components. |
| [Explained delegation to AI managers](explained-delegation.md) | Subsystem managers that learn the player's preferences from their past decisions and explain each action, so delegation scales play without hiding it. |
| [Factories with a living workforce](living-workforce-factories.md) | Automation games whose workers age, learn, form families, and retire, so a production network is also a society that must be sustained across generations. |
| [Generated dream and replay views](dream-replay-layer.md) | Use generative world models for non-authoritative views such as memories, rumors, and alternate histories, where drift is acceptable and variety is the point. |
| [Generated inspection shifts](generated-inspection-shifts.md) | Rule-checking job sims with generated documents, items, and rule changes each shift, verified against an answer key so infinite variety stays fair. |
| [Generated recipe graphs](generated-recipe-graphs.md) | Generate solvable, non-degenerate, on-theme production recipe graphs and tech trees, verified by agents, to cut content cost for factory and crafting games. |
| [Generative decoration catalogs](generative-decoration-catalogs.md) | Let players generate furniture, scenery, and building pieces from text or sketches within a game's style and technical budgets, removing the cap on creative-mode catalogs. |
| [Human-calibrated customers](human-calibrated-customers.md) | Replace hand-tuned customer and crowd preference curves with models that predict human choices, so tycoon markets respond like real populations. |
| [Illustrated chronicles](illustrated-chronicles.md) | Turn a run's event log into a readable, illustrated saga that players can share, making emergent stories legible and portable. |
| [Intent-level orders](intent-level-orders.md) | Players state goals in plain language and the game compiles them into priorities, designations, and schedules, cutting micromanagement in colony and management sims. |
| [Language-agent society terrarium](llm-society-terrarium.md) | An observer-gardener genre where players seed and nudge a persistent society of language-model agents and watch institutions, cultures, and histories form. |
| [Learned build assist for cities](learned-build-assist.md) | Extend Townscaper-style procedural assist to full city builders with learned style priors, so rough strokes become plausible districts the simulation then evaluates. |
| [Learned material surrogates at world scale](learned-material-surrogates.md) | Use learned and GPU-parallel physics surrogates to bring per-particle fluids, gases, and destruction from small arenas to large persistent worlds. |
| [Learned motion for simulated crowds](neural-npc-motion.md) | Physics-based learned character controllers let simulated agents move and react physically, so crowds, injuries, and labor look like what the simulation says is happening. |
| [Learned regional weather](learned-weather-layer.md) | Use machine-learned weather emulators to give farming, flight, and city sims realistic, cheap, regionally coherent weather and climate variability. |
| [Local-first AI simulation games](local-first-ai-sims.md) | Ship small language and generative models inside the game so AI features run offline with no per-hour inference bill, changing the economics of AI-native simulation. |
| [Mean-field crowds and traffic](mean-field-crowds.md) | Simulate hundreds of thousands of agents with equilibrium-consistent route and choice behavior by combining mean-field approximations with sampled individuals. |
| [Mechanic modding by description](language-modding.md) | Players describe a rule change in plain language; a model writes the mod against the modding API and automated agents test it before it is shared. |
| [Natural-language legislation](natural-language-legislation.md) | Players write laws in plain language that are compiled into typed policy parameters, while simulated interest groups argue, lobby, and comply. |
| [Negotiating faction AI](negotiating-faction-ai.md) | Grand strategy rivals that negotiate in language and plan around their promises, combining strategic search with dialogue. |
| [Open-ended evolution sandbox](open-ended-evolution-sandbox.md) | Evolution games built on continuous artificial-life substrates and automated discovery, where morphology and behavior evolve without designer-authored part catalogs. |
| [Parallel autobalancing of economies](parallel-autobalance.md) | Run thousands of scripted, learned, and diversity-seeking agents through a game's economy at accelerated speed to find degenerate strategies and tune parameters before players do. |
| [Participatory planning sandboxes](participatory-planning-sandboxes.md) | City-builder interfaces over calibrated urban models with simulated resident voices, used by communities and planners to explore tradeoffs together. |
| [Placement that tells stories](placement-that-tells-stories.md) | City builders where where and what the player builds triggers specific, state-aware story events about the inhabitants of those buildings. |
| [Quality-diversity scenario libraries](qd-scenario-libraries.md) | Generate large libraries of scenarios that cover a grid of difficulty and play style, so scenario-driven sims never run out of distinct challenges. |
| [Research by named scientists](scientists-not-tech-trees.md) | Replace the abstract research meter with named researchers whose skills, relationships, and rivalries determine what gets discovered and when. |
| [Salience-gated language agents](salience-gated-llm-agents.md) | Keep cheap utility scoring for every tick and call a language model only at salient moments, giving colony and life sims believable minds at a bounded cost. |
| [Simulation games as agent benchmarks](sims-as-agent-benchmarks.md) | Use factory, colony, and economy sims as long-horizon evaluation and training environments for AI agents, with game studios as environment providers. |
| [Simulator instructor coaching](sim-instructor-coach.md) | Flight, driving, and procedure sims with a voice instructor that watches inputs and state, explains mistakes, and adapts lessons in real time. |
| [Specification programming games](specification-programming-games.md) | Programming puzzles where an AI writes the code and the player writes the specification and tests, scored on how precisely the spec pins down correct behavior. |
| [Symbolic simulation, neural rendering](symbolic-sim-neural-render.md) | Keep gameplay in a small deterministic symbolic simulation and let a generative world model render it, decoupling visual variety from simulation cost and art budgets. |
| [Teachable sim companion](teachable-sim-companion.md) | A co-player agent that learns factory, colony, or farm routines from demonstration and language, and grows a library of reusable skills the player can inspect. |
| [Trainable creatures revival](trainable-creatures-revival.md) | Revive the Creatures and Black & White lineage with creatures whose behavior is genuinely learned from player feedback and can explain itself. |
| [Why-query over the simulation log](causal-why-query.md) | Let players ask why something happened and answer from the simulation's own event log, making deep systemic games legible without simplifying them. |
